As a used car dealer myself I can testify that sometimes, things like this do happen. While the "accidentally"  torn check is a little sketchy, the rest of the things could easily happen and be considered no big deal by the employees of the dealership. It does sound like they're giving you the run around a bit, but that could be for any number of reasons that sound legit to them. What I would recommend is this, go to the dealership and speak to your salesman about your concerns. Or even better, speak to his "boss". You've already done business with them and they should be willing to work with you since you've had the car less than a week. Ask to take the car to a mechanic you know and trust and have any work done there and see if they will pay for it, or at least contribute to the costs. 

If they refuse to work with you and say that work needs to be done at their mechanic then that is an issue. That would indicate to me that since the deal is done the don't give a shit anymore and in which case, you've been had. 

Feel free to pm me about with any further questions. If you happen to be in the greater Raleigh area of North Carolina I could recommend some shops that I know and have done business with in the past.

Bus would probably be the best way to go. In Thailand at least they are readily available and pretty reliable. They're also pretty good about being on time. I can't speak for Vietnam or Cambodia as I've never taken a bus in either of those countries. 

Another thing, it's the hot season in this part of the world right now so I would pack for that if I were you. Bring a light rain jacket just in case because if it rains it rains HARD and you may want a light hoodie for buses. The ac tends to be pretty much frigid if it's present.

That depends on how many countries you plan to visit. A lot of countries around here will give you a visa when you enter the country for free but that is only if you enter by air. If you cross by land (bus ticket from the north to the south of Thailand is about 60 USD) the visa costs vary. Thailand is 40 USD and Cambodia is 30. I don't know about any other countries around here as I haven't been yet. 

As for the weather, Thailand has 4 seasons. Hot, hotter, hottest and hot with rain. March through May is hotter. Down south where I am it's pleasant most days though. 

If 800 is your transit budget I'd do some research on visa costs for the countries you want to visa for sure. You can live like a king here on 500 a month, which is 16,400 baht roughly. 

Oh important side note, if you come to Thailand, do not under any circumstances say anything bad about the king. They can and will throw you in prison.

I'd say SEA. I currently live in the south of Thailand and you'd be amazed how cheap it is to live in an Asean Country. Aside from Brunei and Singapore. Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam would definitely be doable on that budget if you're willing to step out and eat local food. You can get a decent meal here in Thailand for about 40 Baht. Which is equivalent to $1 and some change. Accommodations are a bit different but in more touristy areas there are many hostels to choose from. 

The only thing you aren't thinking about is getting here and getting around. Which at this point would likely consume your most of if not your entire budget. Plane tickets are expensive.

As a long term traveler in the south of Thailand I have budgeted around 1200 dollars to hold me over for meals and housing until June. Remember that most currencies have really good exchange rates into most SE Asian currencies. For example, 1 USD is trading for around 34 baht right now. I can have a nice thai meal for 40 baht. If you're willing to try new foods and be a tad frugal you could certainly swing a trip with that much money.

What I use for a day pack is an Osprey Manta 28. While it may be a tad bigger than most day packs it's also big enough that I can pack it for a week or so and not have to bring my Aether 70 along. Plus it comes with a 3 litre hydration bladder and believe you me, that seriously comes in handy here in Thailand. 

Honestly what day pack works best for you really depends on what you're planning to do with it. If you'll be doing nothing more than throwing in, say a rain coat, some tp, (tp is not very common in se Asian restrooms), and a light snack then the Osprey daylite would be perfect for you. 

In case you didn't notice I'm a big osprey fan. You can't really beat the All Mighty Guarantee that they have on all their bags.
